title: Integral compact-support image preserves uniform constructibility

from.place: Proof, sole paragraph: the completed exchange is an isomorphism of integral constructible functors; the constructible landing is the finite-level condition

statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $I=(\varpi)$. Use the completed coefficient sheaves $A_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_T$ and $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $X,Y$ be noetherian schemes (admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) of finite Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $\ell$ invertible on both. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and choose a compactification
$$X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y,\qquad pj=f,$$
with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].
For $T=X,Y$, let $\mathcal C_T=\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be exactly the full category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]: its objects are derived $I$-complete, their normalized reduction towers have common bounded adic-lisse finite-type local models, and they admit compatible etale-origin witnesses. Use its inherited triangulated structure [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated].
Identify $A_{\overline X}|_X=A_X$ by restriction to the open subscheme. Let $j_!$ be exact module extension by zero on this localized ringed site, applied degreewise [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and let $Rp_*$ be the completed-coefficient derived module direct image [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Define $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$, the chosen-compactification candidate [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Then $Rf_!^c$ restricts to an exact $A$-linear functor
$$Rf_!^c:\mathcal C_X\longrightarrow\mathcal C_Y$$
[def-weil-linear-functor, def-weil-triangulated-category]. In particular the output belongs to the full compatible uniform category just specified, including its compatible etale-origin witnesses.

Lemma 6.1.13, Lemma 6.7.2, Definition 6.7.6 and Lemma 6.7.7; completed-coefficient compactification construction and proper preservation. The common-model strengthening uses the existing normalized constructible local-effectivity interface, not an identification by notation.

proof.text:
First check the ambient scheme of the chosen compactification. Properness makes $p$ finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $\overline X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Choose a finite Noetherian affine cover $Y=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}R_i$. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], each inverse image has a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_{ij}$ with a surjection $R_i[t_1,\ldots,t_{r_{ij}}]\twoheadrightarrow B_{ij}$. The affine-cover dimension formula [lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover] and [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] give $\dim R_i\leq D$ for some finite $D\geq0$. By [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension], $\dim R_i[t_1,\ldots,t_{r_{ij}}]\leq D+r_{ij}$. Under a surjection of rings a strict chain of primes in the quotient pulls back to a strict chain of primes, so $\dim B_{ij}\leq D+r_{ij}$. Applying the same affine-cover formulas to $\overline X$ proves that it has finite dimension. These arguments apply to nonempty schemes; an empty scheme already has dimension $-\infty$.
There is also a uniform bound $e=\max(\{0\}\cup\{r_{ij}\})$ on all geometric fibres of $p$. Indeed, for a geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, choose a chart containing its image. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the pullbacks of its source charts are the spectra of $B_{ij}\otimes_{R_i}\Omega$. They cover that fibre and are quotients of $\Omega[t_1,\ldots,t_{r_{ij}}]$: the images of the chosen generators still generate, since every pure tensor is a polynomial in them with coefficients in $\Omega$. A field has only the primes $(0)$ and only the ideals $(0),(1)$, so its dimension is zero and it is Noetherian. The polynomial-dimension theorem, the quotient-chain argument and the affine-cover dimension formulas give dimension at most $e$ for the geometric fibre. Empty charts or fibres contribute $-\infty$ and cause no exception; if $Y$ is empty all three schemes are empty and take $e=0$. Finally $\ell$ is invertible on $\overline X$: at any point the local ring map from $Y$ carries an inverse of $\ell$ to an inverse.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); Tag 0A3V (lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension), with an explicit common-generator proof also for geometric fibres. Schemes Tags 01I4/01JQ, Properties Tag 04MU; polynomial dimension is the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text:
The coefficient facts used below hold for this finite extension: [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] makes $A$ a subring of $E$ and a principal ideal domain with maximal ideal $I$. The extending absolute value is nonarchimedean: after interchanging $x,y$ suppose $|x|_E\leq|y|_E$; if $y\neq0$, then $x/y\in A$ and $1+x/y\in A$, so $|x+y|_E=|y|_E\,|1+x/y|_E\leq|y|_E$, while $y=0$ forces $x=0$. Thus every hypothesis of [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] holds and it makes every $A/I^n$ finite. In particular $A$ is Noetherian, since each ideal has one generator. Also $\ell\in I$: the extending absolute value satisfies $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, so the maximal-ideal description in the first cited statement applies. Fix $K\in\mathcal C_X$ and put $J=j_!K$ in the completed-coefficient derived category of $\overline X$. Apply (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] on $X$: choose its finite stratification and perfect $A$-complex local models. The closed subset $Z=\overline X\setminus j(X)$ has a closed subscheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]; write $i:Z\hookrightarrow\overline X$. Regard each input stratum as a locally closed subscheme of $\overline X$ and add $Z$. For its scheme structure, [def-weil-closed-immersion] factors its immersion into $X$ as a closed immersion followed by an open immersion into $X$. The latter followed by $j$ is open: its image is open in the open $j(X)$ and hence in $\overline X$, and the two structure-sheaf restriction isomorphisms compose, exactly as in [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus the same closed factor followed by this open factor is an immersion into $\overline X$. This is a finite stratification in [def-constructible-stratification]: the strata remain disjoint and cover the open, and $Z$ is their complementary closed stratum.
Use [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] to identify the open site with the localized site in the statement. The completed coefficient identifications on these strata and on their covering objects are the canonical ones of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], applied to $Q_n=A/I^n$; they respect composition. The exact ringed open-closed identities of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] give $j^{-1}J\simeq K$ and $i^{-1}J=0$ on complexes as well: the inverse images are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] and $j_!$ is exact by the same open-closed node. Thus on the old strata $J$ has precisely the original perfect local models, and on $Z$ it has the zero perfect $A$-complex as a model. The coefficient identifications carry $A_X\otimes_A^LP$ to the corresponding model over the restricted $A_{\overline X}$, because restriction here is exact and the bounded finite-projective model is computed termwise. Apply (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] on $\overline X$, whose scheme hypotheses were checked in step 1. It follows that $J\in\mathcal C_{\overline X}$ in the exact sense of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], including common normalized local models and compatible etale-origin witnesses. This argument uses the characterization's stated equivalence, not data from its proof.

proof.text: The same characterization [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], now using (i)$\Rightarrow$(iii), says that $J$ is bounded. Choose $u\leq v$ with $\mathcal H^q(J)=0$ outside $[u,v]$; for the zero object any interval suffices. For every $n\geq1$, [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect] gives the two-term resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A]$ of $P_n=A/I^n$ in degrees $[-1,0]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], its completed constant realization $[A_{\overline X}\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A_{\overline X}]$ is a flat resolution of $(P_n)_{\overline X}$. Consequently the underlying completed-coefficient complex of the canonical reduction $J_n$ is the cone of $\varpi^n:J\to J$. In the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], its degree-$q$ cohomology is between $\mathcal H^q(J)$ and $\mathcal H^{q+1}(J)$, so it vanishes for $q<u-1$ or $q>v$. Restriction of scalar structure does not change a module sheaf's zero object or its cohomology groups. Hence all canonical $J_n$ have the one cohomological interval $[u-1,v]$, independently of $n$.

source.place: Tags 093M (lemma-completion-flat) and 093J (lemma-constant-exact); the stated two-term quotient resolution and the cohomology sequence of its tensor cone. Bhatt-Scholze Proposition 6.8.11(3) supplies the bounded description through the cited characterization.

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible] to the identity base-change square for $p:\overline X\to Y$: both vertical maps are $p$, and the horizontal maps are the identities of $\overline X$ and $Y$. The square is cartesian, and both vertical maps are proper. All four scheme entries are Noetherian and finite-dimensional by step 1 and the hypotheses. Take its integer $N=\ell$: it is positive, kills $A/I$, and is invertible on $Y$ and $\overline X$. The common geometric-fibre bound is the $e$ of step 1. The input $J$ belongs to the exact compatible uniform category by step 2, and its reductions have the common interval $[u-1,v]$ by step 3. Thus the first conclusion of that preservation theorem gives $Rp_*J\in\mathcal C_Y$ (indeed its reductions have cohomology in $[u-1,v+2e]$). This is membership in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], including compatible etale-origin witnesses; it is not just levelwise constructibility. Since $J=j_!K$, [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] identifies this object with precisely the chosen candidate $Rf_!^cK$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, Definition 6.7.6 and Lemma 6.7.7; the precise uniform-and-witness conclusion is the cited existing proper preservation theorem. The finite-level sources are Stacks Tag 0GL0 (theorem-constructible-shriek) and Tag 095U (lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper).

proof.text:
It remains to check functors and exactness, rather than only objects. Exact additive module extension by zero on the localized ringed site is [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] makes its termwise derived functor triangulated. For the direct-image part, the canonical coefficient identification of step 2 gives the ring-sheaf isomorphism required by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with $u=p$, $R_V=A_Y$ and $R_U=A_{\overline X}$. That definition constructs the unbounded derived module direct image by functorial K-injective resolutions in the full module-sheaf category and states that its resolution construction is triangulated, as in [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The completeness and reduction comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] refer to this module direct image; they do not replace its construction. Therefore their composite commutes with shifts and preserves distinguished triangles. Its module direct-image part is additive and $A$-linear on complete objects by [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange], applied to $p$ and the complete object $J$ of step 2.
Extension by zero is $A$-linear as well. For a module-sheaf morphism $t:F\to G$ and a scalar $a\in A$, the functorial direct-sum formula of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] gives $P_{a t}(V)=aP_t(V)$: on the summand indexed by $\varphi:V\to X$ both sides send $s$ to $a\,t_{(V,\varphi)}(s)$. This also covers a zero presheaf value. Write $\eta_F:P_F\to P_F^\#$ and $\eta_G:P_G\to P_G^\#$ for the module sheafification units. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], both $(P_{a t})^\#$ and $a(P_t)^\#$ have precomposite $\eta_G\circ P_{a t}=a(\eta_G\circ P_t)$ with $\eta_F$, since the units are module maps. Uniqueness in that universal property gives $j_!(a t)=a j_!(t)$. Applying this degreewise preserves the equation on cochain maps. The localization functor is $A$-linear by [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. The equation descends to derived morphisms: scalar multiplication on a localized arrow $w^{-1}t$ is $w^{-1}(a t)$, and its image is $(j_!w)^{-1}(a j_!t)=a((j_!w)^{-1}j_!t)$; equivalently use the same identity on composites of chain maps and formal inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. Thus the composite is additive and $A$-linear.
Steps 2 and 4 put its objects in the required full subcategories. Fullness restricts its maps without any choices. By [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated], their shifts and distinguished triangles are inherited from the ambient categories. The preceding shift comparison therefore restricts, and an input distinguished triangle is sent to an ambient distinguished triangle with all three vertices in $\mathcal C_Y$, hence to a distinguished triangle there. This gives the asserted exact $A$-linear functor for the fixed compactification, with no compactification-independence claim needed.
